overall: Tomorrow (July 1) will be an exceptionally hot day in Washington, DC, with an active Heat Advisory in effect through 8:00 PM EDT citing heat index values up to 106°F. The NWS forecasts a high near 98°F with mostly sunny skies and a slight chance (20%) of afternoon thunderstorms after 2 PM, driven by a building heat dome and southwesterly flow.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable model divergence: ECMWF (97.0°F), HRRR (96.5°F), and NBM (94.4°F) cluster in the mid-to-upper 90s and broadly agree, while GFS is a significant cold outlier at ~78.0°F — likely a mesoscale convective or boundary-layer timing issue — which suppresses the full ensemble mean to 93.9°F. Excluding the GFS outlier, the model consensus points firmly to the 94–98°F range.
max_temp_prediction: The weight of evidence from NWS (98°F), ECMWF, HRRR, and NBM strongly favors a high in the 95–98°F range, with the odd-bucket peak at 97–98°F (24.1%) offering the sharpest signal. On the active even-bucket market, the 96–97°F bucket leads at 14.4%, followed by 98–99°F at 9.5%, suggesting a best estimate near 96–97°F; confidence is moderate given GFS drag on the ensemble and the slight storm risk that could briefly cap the afternoon high.
